definition: Active avoidance is a learning and memory task in which a person or animal is exposed to an unpleasant stimulus during training and again during testing. It is used to assess how experience with that negative stimulus affects later performance.

provenance.scope: Source record C226107; pinned source text

reasons: Adds unsupported details not present in the packet, including that the task involves a person or animal and that it is used to assess how experience with the negative stimulus affects later performance.
The packet supports only that it is a task with a negative stimulus in both the learning and memory/testing phases; the broader learning-and-memory explanation is not fully supported as written.

The packet describes an active avoidance task as presenting a negative stimulus during a learning (training) phase and also applying it during a memory (testing) phase, but it does not state that the task is “used to assess how experience with that negative stimulus affects later performance.”
The definition’s claim that it is specifically “a learning and memory task” is not explicitly supported by the packet text beyond the reference to learning (training) and memory (testing) phases.
